# Rush Hour Cluster Analysis Script

This notebook contains code that clones, filters and visualizes an exhaustive dataset of Rush Hour puzzles. Furthermore, the repository also includes a C++ program that can be used to visualize boards within the cluster based on different metrics.

The dataset repository is **public**, therefore the reader is encouraged to clone this colab and run their own scripts. It is recommended to run this script on **Google Colab**.

## Rush Hour

Rush Hour is a puzzle game typically played on a $6\times6$ grid. The objective is to slide the pieces around the board to form an unobstructed path for the red car to reach the exit. The board is populated by up to 12 cars of size $2\times1$ and 4 trucks of size $3\times1$, there is always one piece corresponding to the main red car of size $2\times1$. An example of a board is shown in Figure 1.

## Rush Hour Clusters

A Rush Hour cluster is defined as a group of boards that share the same piece distribution between each other. To analyze the piece distribution of Rush Hour boards, each row and column can be viewed individually, as per Figure 2.

<div align="center">
<img src="data:image/png;base64," width=600>

Figure 2: Indexed piece and type distribution. **Note:** Although possible, rows and columns with the following distributions are arbitrarily not considered due to moving pieces not being possible within them: three $2\times1$ cars; two $3\times1$ trucks.
</div>

Then, by making a combination of 12 values of integer values in the range of 0 and 22, boards can be constructed. By combining the index of types, clusters are obtained, which comprise all boards with a similar board distribution. There are in total $6^{12}$ combinations to describe a cluster, though by the rules of Rush Hour, the third row can only be populated by a single horizontal $2\times1$ car, thereby removing $\frac{1}{6}$ of the combinations.


The accompanying notebook in this repository clones the dataset of `362,797,056` rows, and provides code to analyze the dataset of Rush Hour clusters.
